newsitem.title: USA: Mirage buys land on Atlantic City bordwalk.
newsitem.headline: Mirage buys land on Atlantic City bordwalk.

text.p: Mirage Resorts Inc Chief Financial Officer Dan Lee said the company recently acquired 3.5 acres of land on Atlantic City's boardwalk, bringing the amount of the land it owns on the boardwalk to six acres.
He valued the six acres at as much as $30 million.

"We don't know what we're going to do with it, a joint venture or whatever, but it is one of the few casino sites left along the boardwalk," Lee told investors at the Salomon Brothers Gaming and Lodging Conference here.
In Atlantic City, Mirage is currently developing a huge gambling complex near the city's Marina and is negotiating the construction of a new highway to the site.
Lee said the state of New Jersey might begin building the road by the summer of 1997, in which case Mirage will not begin construction on a hotel until about the same time.
Once construction has started, Lee said a new Mirage resort casino would take about 2.5 years to complete.

In Las Vegas, the company has been planning a new tiger habitat at the Mirage Hotel, and Lee said "it is about ready to go." But he gave no exact date for its opening. Mirage's new Bellagio hotel, currently being built on the Strip in Las Vegas, could be opened as soon as June or July of 1998.
